en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is a critically endangered bird endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
Lake Taal in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a main crater lake inside its volcanic caldera.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral reefs and marine life.
The Philippines is the world's top producer of abaca, a native banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make textiles.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Philippine tarsier, one of the world's smallest primates, has enormous eyes and is native to the islands of Bohol and Samar.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in the provinces of Surigao del Norte and Palawan.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera Administrative Region were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
